decisions.evidence: Risk is the strict-fiber/homotopy-fiber comparison for an arbitrary Serre fibration. I read steps 1.1-2.1: surjectivity lifts the adjointed homotopy over the finite pair (I^n, boundary) with prescribed strict-fiber lift, and injectivity repeats the straightening on the cube I^n x I, where the t=0 slice has constant path coordinate so it stays inside F_b (the text states this slice loosely but the observation is supplied by its own data). Step 1.2's finite-CW compression with the prism identity covers k=0 and k>0, so step 3.1's transfer to j_b and the transport naturality of 4.1 are sound and choice-free.

Risk is the cohomological half. The comparison K_b = j_b^* is an isomorphism by the integral UCT applied to the homology isomorphism, including the Ext term in degree q-1, and the item invokes it with AC declared. The conjugation formulas for homology and cohomology, the reversed path in the cohomological transport, and the empty-fiber, point-fiber, q=0 and zero-ring clauses were checked against the strict-fiber comparison supplier; no cohomological claim is made without the stated AC hypothesis.

Risk is functoriality of the conjugated transport. The proof cancels J_c J_c^{-1} using the middle identity H_q(T_{gamma*eta}) = H_q(T_eta) H_q(T_gamma) from the Hurewicz local system, and in the cohomological branch the path reversal turns T_{bar gamma} into the correct composite so that s_{gamma*eta}=s_eta s_gamma; constants and endpoint-fixed homotopies use the same cited transport laws. No gap found.

Risk is exhaustiveness of the chain filtration, which is claimed only chain-by-chain. The proof cites the compact-CW finite-cell-support lemma to place each simplex image in a finite subcomplex and takes the maximum skeleton over a finitely supported chain, and it explicitly refuses the false degreewise statement F_nC_n = C_n. The cohomological annihilator filtration F^aC^n, the two differential bidegrees and the empty/zero-ring clauses match the standard conventions.

Central risks are the hemisphere suspension, the collar separation, and the identification with cellular chains in the local system. Step 1.1's deformation-retract lifting lemma is correct for Serre fibrations; step 2.1's iterated connecting maps and excision give H_{p+q}(D^p,S^{p-1}) = H_q(F) with orientation sign -1 under reversal; step 2.2's collars, excision and finite additivity are choice-free (finite support only); step 3.1's radial transport and step 4.1's cellular identification are consistent, including p=0 and empty-fiber cases.

Risk is the sign and incidence computation for d_1 = jk. Step 1.1 is the standard exact-couple identification; step 2.1 restricts to each (f,e) component by naturality of connectors and excision; step 3.1's reflection calculation gives -1 for an orientation-reversing incidence and m times the transport for a degree-m incidence, matching the group-ring incidence formula of the local cellular complex. I read the published A^r/B^r definitions and the B^r_{p,q}=A^{r-1}_{p-1,n}+d A^{r-1}_{p+r-1,n+1} formula this proof depends on.

Risks are convergence and the deliberate failure of chain-level degreewise finiteness. Step 1.2 correctly proves F_n H_n = H_n by cellular approximation of one finite representative and a lift; step 2.1's stationary bounds (a-r<0, b-r+1<0) are right; step 3.1 computes E-infinity from the published A^r/B^r formulas, and step 4.1 identifies the quotient with the image filtration in both directions. The simply-connected constant-coefficient clause is standard and the item makes no stronger convergence claim.

Risk is filtration preservation and the homotopy claim on every page. Step 2.2's prism preserves the filtration because the homotopy lies over the fixed cellular map; step 3.3 shows (u_1-u_0)x is an r-boundary by placing P(dx) in the first and Px in the second boundary summand, which I checked against the published C^r formulas; step 3.2's stable/associated-graded comparison is a direct representative check. No gap.

Risk is the domain and target of transgression. I verified that no differential enters (n,0) for 2<=r<=n-1 and none leaves (0,n-1), so D_n=E^n_{n,0} and Q_{n-1}=E^n_{0,n-1} are the surviving subgroup and quotient, that d_n:(n,0)->(0,n-1) is exactly the displayed tau_n with no extra sign, and that the dual cohomological clause is explicitly conditional on a supplied cohomological sequence.

Risk is the identification of the edges and the surjectivity of kappa_b. Naturality against the point fibration and the identity fibration is the right device; step 2.1's direct H_0 computation (each stalk generator is equivalent to an inverse-transported class at b, one path at a time) is correct and shows kappa_b is epic; the augmentation identification in 2.2 needs every fiber nonempty and path connected exactly as stated. No defect.

Risk is the identity tau_n(xi)=q_n delta[x]. I checked A^n_{n,n}=C_n(E_n) cap d^{-1}C_{n-1}(E_0), that x is a relative cycle for (E_n,E_0), and that the target quotient B^n_{0,n-1}=d(A^{n-1}_{n-1,n}) contains d a for a in A^{n-1}_{n-1,n}, which is exactly what step 3.1's representative-independence argument needs. Step 2.1's sign is fixed by the same boundary convention as the differential. No gap.

Risks are relative vanishing H_k(E,E_m)=0 for k<=m, the splitting of the product cochain complex, and the finite-quotient convergence comparison. Step 1.2's finite cellular approximation with lifting is correct; step 2.1's primitive choice in the product complex is the genuine AC use it declares and avoids the Milnor lim^1 failure by choosing primitives coordinatewise; step 2.2 applies the UCT under AC, and step 3.2/4.2 use N=2n+3 with the finite-window clause of the published definition.

Risk is the containment bookkeeping that makes the page products well defined and the derivation rule. I rechecked steps 1.1, 2.1 and 2.2: products of A^r numerators land in A^r, products with the A^{r-1} summand land in the target B^r summands, and (du)y and u(dy) land in the required filtration ranges. The E-infinity product is then the associated-graded product under the stated degreewise-finite hypothesis, and no choice is used.

Risk is the construction of filtered products, since the item itself shows the raw cup need not respect the skeletal filtration. The filtered diagonal comes from a cellular diagonal of the base lifted through the Hurewicz replacement, the relative external product is justified by an explicit open triad, and steps 5.1-7.1 ascend the paired exact couple to all pages; step 8.1's sign (-1)^{bc} and the reverse transport on the back face are internally consistent with the cited local-coefficient cup. Residual uncertainty is confined to the sign conventions of the two published suppliers this proof cites for relative products.

Risk is the equivalence between support separation and collapse. The endpoint argument is correct: zero terms persist, so a differential with a source or target outside S_r is zero; homological differentials lower total degree by one and cohomological ones raise it, so single-parity support kills every differential and the local criterion follows. The item correctly refuses the converse and cites the internal nonsplitting witness rather than asserting one.

Risks are the two-row collapse and the sign in d_{n+1}(au)=(-1)^{|a|} a cup e. Only rows 0 and n carry the constant group R, so for 2<=s<=n every differential has a zero endpoint and the only surviving one is d_{n+1}:(a,n)->(a+n+1,0); the Leibniz rule with |u|=n gives the stated sign, and step 4.1's splice of kernel and cokernel into the two-piece filtration gives the exact sequence. No defect.

Risk is the one-cell cellular local boundary and the kernel-cokernel splice. With the fixed positive-edge convention the local differential is 1-T_q, giving E^2_{0,q}=coker(1-T_q) and E^2_{1,q}=ker(1-T_q); support in two columns kills every d_r with r>=2, and the resulting short exact sequence with 1-T_{q-1} on the right reproduces the Wang sequence. Orientation reversal changes the sign exactly as stated. The owning contract's templated iff-reverse boundary row was also made item-specific; recorded as defect row 5a-b-007.

Risk is the claimed classification of the examples. I checked that torsion and p-primary torsion are closed under tensor and Tor with an arbitrary group (a common integer, respectively power of p, kills every elementary tensor and every Tor class), so they are Serre ideals, and that the explicit witnesses D=oplus_j Z/n show finite and finitely generated groups fail the ideal property while remaining Serre rings. The kernel-cokernel sequence (1) supports the two-out-of-three and composition claims.

Risk is the filtered-morphism clause. The induction from f_{-1}:0->0 through the snake sequence is correct: if f_{i-1} and gr_i(f) are C-isomorphisms, the snake sequence expresses ker f_i and coker f_i as extensions of subquotients of four C groups, and closure under extensions gives the conclusion; the membership clause is the defining extension closure. No gap, and no choice is used.

Risks are the backwards differential-closure set and the C-isomorphism transfer. The recursion T_s = T_{s+1} union its two differential translates is exactly what places the three-term complex of each x in T_s, step 1.2's image/kernel argument is a valid kernel-cokernel square chase, and every point of total degree at most N is stable at page R=N+2. The item states no converse, and its object clause is the standard finite-filtration induction.

Risks are the base-edge kernel/cokernel control in clause 1 and the relative quotient filtration in clause 2. In clause 1 the ideal property puts every E^2_{s,t} with t>0 in C, the edge kernel is filtered by positive-t stable pieces, and the cokernel has successive quotients inside C; in clause 2 every off-bottom term in total degree i<=n has s>=2 and 1<=t<=n-2, so tensor and Tor of Serre-ring elements lie in C. The stated degree ranges are respected.

Risk was the transfer citation: the cited bounded-transfer theorem requires every E^2 term with p+q<=N to lie in the class, but E^2_{0,0}=Z is outside the torsion and p-primary classes. I repaired step 2.1 to record the axis terms E^2_{s,0}=H_s(B) and E^2_{0,t}=H_t(F) for s,t>0 and to apply the transfer argument on the positive-total-degree region, noting that the isolated (0,0) term has no outgoing first-quadrant differential and contributes only to H_0. The four closure classes and both edge forms are unchanged. Repair recorded in defect row 5a-b-006.

Risk is the PID Tor finite-generation step and the filtration assembly. Step 1.1 is correct: a finitely generated PID module is a finite sum of free and cyclic torsion summands, Tor_1(R/(a),G)=ker(a:G->G) is a submodule of the Noetherian finitely generated G, and finite additivity gives the claim. The UCT then makes every E^2 term in the triangle finitely generated, submodules and quotients stay finitely generated, and the finite abutment filtration gives H_n.

Risk is the CW-homotopy-type claim for the strict loop fiber. The circle half is a direct covering and long-exact-sequence argument; for the path fibration the long exact sequence identifies the loop fiber with a K(A,n-1) up to weak equivalence, and the recorded Schoen proposition supplies CW homotopy type so that Eilenberg-Mac Lane uniqueness applies. Marked uniqueness and the AC bookkeeping are stated explicitly, and A=0 is covered.

Risk is the induction and the odd case's multi-row bookkeeping. The even case forces d_j to be an isomorphism at every base degree, giving Q[x_j]; the odd case uses d_j(y^k)=k y^{k-1}x_j, x_j^2=0 (odd total degree over Q), and a least-counterexample argument showing no later differential can hit a nonzero bottom-row class, so A=Lambda(x_j). I verified the two inputs of the minimality step: A^q=0 for 0

Risk is the integral ring statement. The two-row sequence of the contractible path fibration forces multiplication by c=d_2(u) to be injective and surjective in every base degree; from A^0=Z one gets A^2=Zc and A^1=0, and the induction gives Z[c] with no extension ambiguity because each total degree has a single filtration quotient. The transgression sign and the effect of reversing u are stated explicitly.

Risks are the explicit charts/numerations and the forced two-row isomorphisms. I checked the affine charts and the partition functions (some |z_j|^2 >= 1/(n+1) forces a positive denominator and supports inside U_j); the CW structure has one cell in each even degree so all cellular differentials vanish; the total sphere has cohomology only in degrees 0 and 2n+1, forcing d_2 to be an isomorphism for 0<=p<2n and leaving u x^n as the top survivor. This item also received the LaTeX repair recorded in defect row 5a-b-001.

Risks are the right-scalar chart convention and the two-row computation. The charts use right multiplication consistently, the partition functions are the same support-subordinate data, and the CW structure has one cell in each degree divisible by four; rows 0 and 3 force d_4 to be an isomorphism for 0<=p<4n and leave u x^n as the top survivor, with x^{n+1}=0 by dimension. This item also received the LaTeX repair recorded in defect row 5a-b-002. The owning contract's templated iff-reverse boundary row was also made item-specific; recorded as defect row 5a-b-008.

Risk is the direction of the kernel and cokernel vanishings. With columns 0 and N the sole differential is d_N:G_q->G_{q+N-1}; its kernel vanishes because the source's stable term is zero and its cokernel vanishes because the target has positive total degree, giving G_q = G_{q+2m}; G_j=0 for 0<j<2m follows since no differential can enter (0,j). The item states an additive calculation only and makes no Pontryagin-ring claim.

Risk is identifying monodromy with the gluing homeomorphism. The chart description across the seam and the lift of the positive loop give T_q=f_*; the five-term Wang segment then yields the stated kernel-cokernel short exact sequence with no splitting claim. The q=0 case, the identity monodromy, empty F and the orientation-sign substitution are all covered explicitly. The owning contract's templated iff-reverse boundary row was also made item-specific; recorded as defect row 5a-b-009.

Risk is the claimed filtration. Using the homotopy exact sequence of the mapping-path fibration of the quotient map BZ->BC_n I verified pi_1(F)=nZ, pi_k(F)=0 for k>1, H_1(E)=Z by Hurewicz, and that the edge image gives 0 < nZ < Z with stable pieces nZ and Z/n. Nonsplitting is then the standard argument that Z/n does not embed in the torsion-free group Z.

Risk is the local boundary 1-T with T=-1 in fiber degree one. Reflection acts by -1 on H_1(S^1), so the one-cell local differential is 2, giving E^2_{0,1}=Z/2 and E^2_{1,1}=0 while the false constant table would give Z in both; the mapping-torus Wang sequence and the explicit fixed-point section give H_1(K)=Z oplus Z/2, so the torsion summand is exactly what the untwisted table misses.

Read in full. Transport along a path is represented by a map of fibers whose composite with the target inclusion is homotopic to the source inclusion, so each named class pulls back to itself; the transport matrix in the supplied basis is therefore the identity for every path class, giving the constant system. No path-connected base is needed, and AC enters only through the cohomological transport supplier.

Risk is the passage from an associated-graded isomorphism to an isomorphism of the actual filtered map. Phi is filtered because a pullback class sits in the Serre filtration of its base degree and cupping with a fixed class cannot lower it; the published finite-complete-filtration lifting lemma then applies degree by degree. No splitting or complement is chosen, and the item is stated conditionally on gr Phi being an isomorphism.

Risk is the identification of the E_2 map and the lifting step. Under the supplied global basis the fiber system is constant, the classes e_i are permanent cycles, and the induced E_2 map is the basis map, hence an isomorphism in every bidegree; the associated-graded lemma then gives the actual cup-product isomorphism, which is an H^*(B;R)-module map and natural for maps carrying the chosen classes. No extension ambiguity remains.

Read in full. Disk, sphere and Thom space are defined from a supplied metric; the radial comparison r_{h,k} is a base-preserving homeomorphism of pairs (continuity at the zero section from the locally bounded ratio of norms) with the interpolation giving a radial isotopy; rank zero (S empty, Th=B_+) and the empty-base quotient are handled.

Read in full. Rank zero gives D=B and S empty, hence Th=B_+; the product bundle has (D,S)=(BxD^n,BxS^{n-1}) and collapsing the second subspace gives B_+ wedge S^n = Sigma^n B_+; n=0 and B empty reduce to the stated conventions, and every map is the identity formula, so naturality is immediate.

Risk is the arbitrary-R computation that replaced an earlier Z/F_2-only supplier. The Mayer-Vietoris suspension recursion computes reduced sphere cohomology over any commutative ring, and the pair sequence gives H^n(D^n,S^{n-1};R)=R with the ordered orientation generator; a linear automorphism of the disk pair acts by a unit because a rank-one module automorphism is multiplication by a unit. Only fixed finite covers occur, so the calculation is choice-free.

Risk is well-definedness of the rank-one local system. Transition functions act on the top relative group by the unit induced by the disk-pair automorphism, these units are locally constant and satisfy the cocycle law, and metric changes are absorbed by the canonical radial pair isomorphisms. The integral sign obstruction over a loop, the canonical mod-two orientation, the rank-zero single orientation and the empty-base clause are all stated correctly.

Read in full. A normalized Thom class is defined by the fiber restrictions i_b^*u=o_b in relative singular cochains, with existence and uniqueness explicitly deferred to later items; empty base, rank zero and the zero ring are listed, and no representative is selected, so the definition is choice-free.

Risk is the sign of the iterated suspension generators. The interval case computes the connector as the cokernel of the diagonal and identifies it with the boundary-difference class; the relative cup formula contributes the unit (-1)^{|a|}, and the ordered iterated connectors generate the disk-pair group over an arbitrary commutative ring, so cup by u=pr_2^*v_n is an isomorphism with the stated normalization.

Risk is the Mayer-Vietoris ladder and uniqueness. The relative small-chain MV sequence is justified by subdivision, the four outer vertical cup maps are the stipulated local isomorphisms, and the five lemma gives the middle one; uniqueness follows because u-u'=pi^*a cup u with a in H^0, and fiber normalization forces a to vanish on every component. Empty-open degenerations and rank zero are covered.

Read in full. The finite induction glues W_j with U_{j+1} through the two-open lemma; compatibility on the overlap holds because both restrictions are normalized for the same supplied orientation and are equal by uniqueness; the induction is finite and depends only on the supplied enumeration, so no choice is needed. Empty and repeated members and m=0,1 are covered.

Risk is running the Serre construction on relative cochains and reading the edge as cup with u. The relative cell quotient preserves the fibration lifting and subdivision, the fiber term is H^q(D^n,S^{n-1};R), so a supplied orientation leaves a single row and there are no extensions; the surviving unit defines a normalized class by cellwise restriction, and the edge is the product with it. The paracompact CW-type branch transports along a homotopy equivalence with its homotopy inverse.

Risk is uniqueness and the twisted form. Both follow from the one-row edge: normalized classes differ by pi^*a with a in H^0 vanishing at every fiber generator, and without a trivialized orientation the same collapse gives H^k(B;O_R(xi)) = H^{k+n}(D,S). The finite-cover theorem is identified with the Serre class by uniqueness rather than treated as an additional hypothesis.

Risk is the pullback and orientation-reversal clauses. The pulled-back class restricts to the prescribed generator on every fiber because the pullback orientation preserves that generator, so uniqueness identifies it with the Thom class of the pullback; replacing an integral generator by its negative makes -u normalized for the reversed orientation, and uniqueness gives the stated negation. Rank zero and empty-base cases are literal.

Risk is the radial identification of the product pair with the sum-metric pair and the Koszul sign. The radial homeomorphism between the max-norm and sum-norm unit pairs is continuous at the zero section; the product generator is the ordered generator, giving u_{xi x eta}=u_xi x u_eta; diagonal pullback gives the Whitney-sum formula; swapping the blocks crosses n degree-one connectors past m, contributing (-1)^{nm}.

Risk is well-definedness of the Thom diagonal and the conditional collapse. Sphere points map to the basepoint independently of the base coordinate, so the quotient universal property applies; the zero section is continuous in charts and a section; the collapse is defined only for supplied tubular data and no tubular-neighborhood existence theorem is asserted. Rank zero reduces to the ordinary based diagonal.

Risk is the composite s^* j^* u. It is defined without any later characteristic-class page; naturality of the pair sequence and of the Thom class gives e(f^*xi)=f^*e(xi), orientation reversal negates the class, and rank zero gives e=1. The definition is choice-free once u is supplied, with AC inherited only from general Thom existence and naturality.

Risk is the displayed identity s^* s_!(a)=a cup e. The radial homotopy retracts D(xi) to the zero section, so s^* is an isomorphism; cup-product naturality with s^* pi^* = id and the definition of the Euler class give the identity. Rank zero, empty base, the zero ring and negative-degree inputs are covered literally.

Risk is that rewriting the disk/sphere pair sequence really yields the displayed Gysin sequence and that the Euler class is the transgression. I checked the identifications H^k(D,S)=H^{k-n}(B) and H^k(D)=H^k(B), under which the relative-to-absolute map becomes multiplication by e; the comparison with the sphere-fiber Serre transgression is carried out in cochains for n>=2, and rank one is explicitly excluded from that comparison.

Risk is the composite normal bundle and the two-stage pushforward. Pullback commutes with pi^*, the relative cup and the pair map, giving naturality; in ordered tubular coordinates the composite normal directions are those of xi and then s_xi^*eta, and associativity of the cup product identifies (s_eta)_!(s_xi)_! with the pushforward of the ordered normal sum. The Koszul convention explains why the summand order is stated.

Read in full. The classes 1xb_i restrict to b_i on every fiber, so the global-basis hypothesis holds; the Leray-Hirsch map is sum a_i x b_i, which is the finite-free Kunneth cross-product isomorphism, so the two isomorphisms agree as maps and not merely abstractly. The basis is supplied and AC is inherited from Kunneth and Leray-Hirsch.

Risk is only the specialization of the trivial-bundle theorems. Ranks one and two give the once- and twice-suspended units, the generators are the ordered relative connectors, and the Thom isomorphisms are the relative suspension isomorphisms over an arbitrary commutative ring. Empty-base, point-base and coordinate-order cases are explicit.

Risk is the monodromy computation. The clutching reflection swaps the endpoint coordinates and sends (0,1) to -(0,1) modulo the diagonal, so the integral orientation monodromy is -1 and no global integral generator exists; modulo two the sign degenerates, the canonical F_2-orientation applies, and the Thom theorem gives the degree-one isomorphism. The model and the clutching action are stated explicitly.

Risk is orientation and numerability. The complex structure gives positive-determinant transitions because multiplication by z has determinant |z|^2, and the principal S^1 charts of the Milnor model numerate the line bundle, so the general Thom theorem applies with R=Z and n=2. No Euler or characteristic-class identification is used, and AC is spent only through the Thom theorem.

Risk is the actual group H^1(K). Reflection monodromy is -1, so no global integral fiber basis exists (the contrapositive of the global-basis lemma); Wang gives 0 -> Z/2 -> H_1(K) -> Z -> 0, split by the fixed-point section, and the UCT with H_0 free gives H^1(K)=Hom(Z oplus Z/2,Z)=Z rather than the Z^2 predicted by a falsely constant table. The two bundles compared are the reflexion mapping torus and the product.

Risk is the contradiction argument. Pulling the disk pair back over the interval parameter and comparing the two endpoint inclusions (homotopic through maps of pairs) gives j_0^*Q^*u=j_1^*Q^*u, while the clutching relation and the reflection sign give g=-g; torsion-freeness of Z forces g=0, contradicting that g is a generator. The mod-two positive case is the contrasting statement, and AC enters only through the positive existence clause.

Read the A-page prose against its 25 manifest items. Every paragraph claim was matched to an authored item: the strict-fiber/homotopy-fiber separation and local-system transport, the choice-free homological branch versus the AC-bearing cohomological comparison, the relative-cell and d_1 calculation, the naturality and convergence claims, the coefficient-carrying edge maps and transgression, the multiplicative structure, the collapse criteria with the explicit nonsplitting warning, the Serre-class ring/ideal split, and the Eilenberg-Mac Lane computation. No page-level claim exceeds the authored items and no unsupported statement was found.

Read the B-page prose against its 7 itemized examples and counterexamples. The CP-infinity, complex and quaternionic Hopf, odd-sphere loop-space and mapping-torus descriptions match the authored statements, including the additive-only loop-space claim and the no-splitting warning; the counterexample paragraph matches the realized nonsplit filtration 0 in nZ in Z and the Klein-bottle torsion Z/2 under reflection monodromy. Consistent.

Read the A-page prose against its 20 items: the global-basis hypothesis and monodromy trivialization, the filtered lifting without splittings, the metric disk/sphere/Thom construction, the arbitrary-R disk-pair computation, the orientation system and fiberwise normalization, the trivial, finite-cover and numerable Thom theorems, naturality and uniqueness, the Euler class, the zero-section pushforward and the pair-sequence Gysin ladder, and pullback/composition compatibility. The rank restrictions on the Serre comparison are stated as in the items.

Read the B-page prose against its 6 items: the product-bundle Leray-Hirsch/Kunneth agreement, the suspended Thom spaces of trivial line and plane bundles, the Mobius sign computation and its mod-two contrast, the tautological complex line over CP-infinity, and the two counterexamples (no global integral fiber basis over the Klein bottle; no integral Thom class without orientation). Consistent with the authored statements.

Read in full. The definition fixes fiberwise-linear charts, the transition convention g_{ki}=g_{kj}g_{ji}, fixed rank, n=0 as X->X, the empty base and numerability via a linear trivializing cover with a subordinate locally finite partition of unity. It is exactly the interface the cocycle, pullback and metric items consume.

Risk is the derivation of DC from AC. The successor sets S_u are nonempty by entirety, one choice function on the family {S_u} defines s(u)=c(S_u) with u R s(u), and recursion from the prescribed initial point gives the required sequence; this is the standard argument, it spends AC exactly once, and it is what licenses later items to discharge their separately declared DC hypotheses.

Read in full. The cocycle makes the gluing relation reflexive, symmetric and transitive (g_{ij}g_{ji}=I, transitivity from the cocycle law); the charts Phi_i are well defined and continuous by the quotient property with continuous inverse; gauge changes h_i give isomorphic bundles, and every bundle is recovered from any linear atlas. No gap.

Read in full. Bundle maps over a base map, isomorphisms over the identity, sections (with the nowhere-zero condition), and the rank-r subbundle condition requiring local product charts are stated, so constant fiber dimension is explicitly insufficient; the short exact sequence conventions include the subbundle structures on kernel and image.

Read in full. The pullback is the subspace of XxE over the graph of f with fiberwise operations; a linear chart pulls back to f^{-1}(U)xF^n, so it is a vector bundle; the canonical map to E is a bundle map over f, and sections pull back by x|->(x,s(f(x))).

Read in full. The identity and composite comparisons are explicit mutually inverse fiberwise-linear continuous maps that delete redundant base coordinates; coherence for three composable base maps and naturality for bundle maps hold because every route ends at the same pair, and the pullback section formula respects identities and composition under these comparisons.

Read in full. Each operation is defined by its transition matrices (diagonal sum, tensor, inverse-transpose dual, conjugation action on Hom, exterior power) and glued by the cocycle theorem; the fibers, Lambda^0, Lambda^k=0 for k>rank, the conjugate and realification constructions, and commutation with pullback are stated. No hidden choice.

Risk is continuity of the summed metric and the use of the partition theorem. Terms are zero-extended off U_i, so continuity holds near the complement and local finiteness bounds the sum; at each x some rho_i(x)>0 and the corresponding transported Euclidean or Hermitian form is positive definite, giving strict positivity and the sesquilinearity laws. AC/DC is spent only to obtain the numeration, and with supplied data the construction is choice-free.

Read in full. Given a metric, the orthogonal complement C=i(E')^perp is a subbundle by a graph-of-continuous-linear-map argument in an adapted local frame, q|_C is a bundle isomorphism by finite-dimensional injectivity, and the sum map is a bundle isomorphism by local direct-sum frames. The splitting depends on the metric, as stated.

Risk is the embedding and the complementary subbundle. The square-root-weighted chart formula is injective because some rho_i(x)>0, and the orthogonal projection onto the image plane varies continuously via (A^*A)^{-1}; the complementary projections have locally constant rank mn-n, which the subbundle criterion turns into a subbundle. Empty base and rank zero use N=0, and the finite cover comes from compactness plus the partition corollary.

Risk is the endpoint transport from a numeration over X x I. Compactness of I makes the pullback trivial over a neighborhood of each x after pasting strip trivializations; the countable countabilization and locally finite partition produce finitely many graph isomorphisms whose composite is locally constant in the index; the resulting endpoint isomorphism is explicit and no canonicity is claimed. The proof shape is the standard one and the AC use is exactly the countabilization.

Read in full. The frame bundle is a principal GL_n-bundle via linear charts and evaluation gives the canonical isomorphism of the associated bundle with E; numerations correspond in both directions and n=0 gives singletons. Consistent with the principal-bundle supplier it cites.

Read in full. The orientation cover, orientation as a section, orientation-preserving maps, the positive frame bundle as a GL_n^+-subbundle, and the H-reduction convention are stated; rank zero has a single canonical orientation, and no metric or choice is used in this construction.

Read in full. Positive orthonormal frames give an SO(n)-reduction in oriented orthonormal charts; conversely an SO(n)-reduction orients each fiber and a local section makes the orientation continuous; the constructions are inverse, and orientation-preserving isometries (or polar normalization of a general orientation-preserving isomorphism) transport the reductions. n=0 is included.

Risk is the topology and the colimit conventions. The graph charts trivialize V_n -> Gr_n as a principal K_n-bundle, so the associated standard bundle is exactly the tautological bundle; the stable colimit uses the weak direct-limit topology, later identified with the CW topology by the Schubert theorem, and n=0 gives points, points and the zero bundle. No classification claim is made in the definition itself.

Risk is the double-cover claim and the BSO model. Frames modulo SO(n) are exactly oriented planes; forgetting the orientation is two-to-one for n>=1 because a positive-dimensional real space has exactly two orientations; the tautological oriented bundle pulls back to the unoriented tautological bundle, and BSO(n) is introduced as a chosen model rather than a new theorem.

Risk is continuity of the image-plane map and the numeration clause. The projection P=A(A^*A)^{-1}A^* is continuous and determines the plane locally; the weighted chart formula embeds E into finitely or countably many coordinates with local finiteness; the tautological pullback identification e|->(p(e),j(e)) is a bundle isomorphism because (A^*A)^{-1}A^* varies continuously. Compact bases use the finite complement theorem for a finite embedding.

Risk is the converse direction. Homotopic maps give isomorphic pullbacks by endpoint transport; conversely an isomorphism Phi lets one substitute the odd and even coordinate embeddings and interpolate the fibers by cos(theta) O(j_0 v)+sin(theta) P(j_1 Phi v), which is injective because the two terms lie in orthogonal coordinate subspaces. Concatenating the two displacement homotopies proves f_0 homotopic to f_1 without paracompactness.

Risk is well-definedness on homotopy classes and surjectivity. Surjectivity uses the numerated embedding; well-definedness uses the converse lemma, which needs no paracompactness, so the bijection holds for paracompact Hausdorff CGWH bases and for any CGWH base with numerability supplied. The stable Grassmannian is paracompact and the tautological bundle numerable, and nonnumerable bundles are explicitly excluded.

Risk is the oriented analogue. The transported image orientation varies continuously in oriented frames, giving a map to the oriented Grassmannian; homotopic maps give orientation-preserving endpoint isomorphisms because every transition matrix has positive determinant, and the converse interpolation runs through oriented planes. The SO(n)-reduction reading is supplied by the orientation/metric proposition, and n=0 gives singletons.

Collar neighborhoods of the equator give two open product charts whose transition is the given g, so the gluing theorem applies; the upper-to-lower convention is fixed and stated to yield the tautological Hopf line for g(z)=z, and swapping the two charts replaces g by g^{-1}. Rank zero gives the unique zero bundle.

The disk argument uses a finite trivializing cover, the projection-gap subdivision and injective projections of equal rank; the gauge criterion h=A_- g A_+^{-1} is exactly equivalent to an isomorphism of the clutched bundles; the ranges come from the last-column fibrations U(n)->U(n+1)->S^{2n+1} and O(n)->O(n+1)->S^n. Rank zero gives one class.

Risk is the long-line argument. The tangent bundle of the smooth long line is locally trivial over a CGWH nonmetrizable base; if it were numerable it would carry a metric, and the induced length metric would give a metric inducing the topology, contradicting nonmetrizability; a pullback of the numerable tautological line would have to be numerable. The long line's differentiability and nonmetrizability are recorded from the cited source.
